For a quadratic \(h(x)=\frac12x^THx\),

\[
P_{h,\rho}(v)=(H+\rho I)^{-1}\rho v.
\]

Put \(t=\rho\). Then

\[
A:=P_{f,\rho}=\begin{bmatrix}
\frac{t}{t+1}&0\\
0&\frac{t}{t+4}
\end{bmatrix}.
\]

The matrix \(R\) has eigenvalues \(1,4\) in the directions \((1,1)\) and \((1,-1)\), so

\[
B:=P_{g,\rho}
=\frac12
\begin{bmatrix}
a+b&a-b\\
a-b&a+b
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
a=\frac{t}{t+1},\quad b=\frac{t}{t+4}.
\]

The Douglas-Rachford update is linear:

\[
z^+=Mz,\qquad M=I+\theta N,
\]

where

\[
N=B(2A-I)-A.
\]

A direct simplification gives

\[
N=
\begin{bmatrix}
-\frac{t(7t+13)}{2(t+1)^2(t+4)}
&
\frac{3t(t-4)}{2(t+1)(t+4)^2}
\\[4pt]
\frac{3t(t-1)}{2(t+1)^2(t+4)}
&
-\frac{t(13t+28)}{2(t+1)(t+4)^2}
\end{bmatrix}.
\]

Since \(C(\rho,\theta)=\|M\|_2\), we use

\[
\|M\|_2^2\ge \frac12\|M\|_F^2.
\]

Now

\[
\frac12\|I+\theta N\|_F^2
=
1+\theta\operatorname{tr}N+\frac{\theta^2}{2}\|N\|_F^2.
\]

For fixed \(t\), this quadratic is minimized at

\[
\theta=-\frac{\operatorname{tr}N}{\|N\|_F^2},
\]

so for every \(\theta\),

\[
C(\rho,\theta)^2
\ge
1-\frac{(\operatorname{tr}N)^2}{2\|N\|_F^2}.
\]

Writing all entries over the common denominator \(2(t+1)^2(t+4)^2\), one obtains the exact identity

\[
81\|N\|_F^2-41(\operatorname{tr}N)^2
=
\frac{t^2(t-2)^2(679t^2+2306t+2716)}
{(t+1)^4(t+4)^4}.
\]

Since \(t>0\), the right side is nonnegative, with equality only at \(t=2\). Hence

\[
\frac{(\operatorname{tr}N)^2}{\|N\|_F^2}\le \frac{81}{41},
\]

and therefore

\[
C(\rho,\theta)^2\ge 1-\frac12\cdot\frac{81}{41}
=\frac1{82}.
\]

Now check attainability. At \(t=2\),

\[
A=\begin{bmatrix}2/3&0\\0&1/3\end{bmatrix},
\]

and

\[
N=
\begin{bmatrix}
-\frac12&-\frac1{18}\\[2pt]
\frac1{18}&-\frac12
\end{bmatrix}.
\]

Thus

\[
M=
\begin{bmatrix}
1-\theta/2&-\theta/18\\
\theta/18&1-\theta/2
\end{bmatrix},
\]

so

\[
\|M\|_2^2
=
\left(1-\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\theta}{18}\right)^2.
\]

This is minimized at

\[
\theta=\frac{81}{41},
\]

which lies in \((0,2)\), and the minimum value is

\[
\left(\frac1{82}\right)^2+\left(\frac9{82}\right)^2
=
\frac1{82}.
\]

Therefore

\[
C_*=\frac1{\sqrt{82}}.
\]

The equality conditions above force \(t=2\) and then force \(\theta=81/41\), so the minimizing pair is unique.

\[
\boxed{\left(2,\frac{81}{41},\frac1{\sqrt{82}}\right)}
\]
